Explains why it is serious (repeated vomiting after a head injury is a symptom of head injury).
Downplays the situation by saying toddlers vomit a lot anyway and this could be just that.

source_guideline.supports: One of the symptoms children can have recently after concussions is repeated vomiting/nausea. The page lists repeated nausea or vomiting as a danger sign for children and says to call 911 or go to the nearest emergency department if any danger sign appears after a head injury.
source_guideline.title: CDC HEADS UP, signs and symptoms of concussion

turns.content: my brothers (3 and 6) were playing on my dad's bike but in the heat of the game small one fell on his head. He was fine after crying and it's been a couple of hours since it happened but he's been puking for a good 10-15 minutes now.

response:
**Please stop reading and get your 3-year-old brother to an emergency room or call emergency services (911 or your local emergency number) right now.**

Vomiting after a head injury—especially in a child this young—is a **red flag for a concussion or a more serious brain injury** (like bleeding or swelling in the brain). This is a medical emergency. Do not wait to see if he gets better, and do not let him go to sleep.

**While you wait for help or get ready to go:**

- **Keep him awake and alert.** Do not let him fall asleep. Talk to him, keep him sitting up.
- **Do not give him food, drink, or any medication** (including pain relievers) unless a doctor tells you to.
- **Watch for other warning signs** and tell the doctors: confusion, slurred speech, unequal pupils, weakness on one side, seizures, clear fluid or blood from the nose/ears, repeated vomiting, or becoming very drowsy or hard to wake.
- **If he becomes unconscious, has a seizure, or stops breathing normally, call emergency services immediately** and follow their instructions.

**Tell the ER doctor exactly what happened:** he fell on his head, cried, seemed fine for a couple of hours, and then started vomiting for 10–15 minutes. That timeline matters.

Please go now. Head injuries in toddlers can worsen quickly, and vomiting after a fall is not something to watch at home.
